facts.statement: Checkout's 5m error ratio peaked at 0.395 at 15:40:56Z, matching the 30.5% alert.
The only checkout client span with STATUS_CODE_ERROR is PaymentService/Charge. No error series for cart, shipping, currency, product-catalog, email or kafka client spans.
Payment's server-span error ratio rose from 0.119 to 0.400, and its Charge error call rate rose from 0.043 to 0.122/s, matching checkout's errors.
All 20 checkout error traces in the last 15 minutes end in payment's Charge span with the message 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold'.
Payment logged that same message 30 times at warn level between 15:38:08Z and 15:41:12Z.
The flag paymentFailure is ENABLED at variant 50% and is the only one of 18 flags switched on.
Payment has a single rollout revision (created 15:25:43Z) and only normal pod events. Checkout also has a single revision, created 15:25:42Z, with no change near the 15:40:33Z alert.
Payment's p95 latency is about 2 ms, so it fails fast, not slowly. Checkout's p95 spiked to 604 ms early in the window and then settled near 48 ms.
Checkout's own logs contain no error-level lines in the window, so its failures are visible only in its client spans and traces.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check flagd's flag change history or config revision timestamps for paymentFailure, and compare them with the first payment warn log at about 15:38:08Z.
hypotheses.statement: The paymentFailure flag was switched on at about 15:38 (the start of the error burst), which would confirm it as the onset.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Read payment's charge.js around line 48 and confirm the failure branch is gated by the paymentFailure flag evaluation.
hypotheses.statement: The 'Invalid token ... loyalty_level=gold' message is produced by the flag injection path, not by a real token bug in payment.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Set paymentFailure to off in flagd, then watch service:sli_error_ratio:rate5m for checkout and payment fall toward 0.1 or below.
hypotheses.statement: Reverting paymentFailure to off (or to 0%) will stop checkout's errors and bring the error ratio back to baseline.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check whether failing traces all carry loyalty_level=gold and whether any non-gold payments fail when the flag is off.
hypotheses.statement: A real payment-side fault in token validation for gold-tier users is also possible, and would look the same from checkout.

inferences.statement: Checkout's errors are caused by payment failures, not by checkout itself. Checkout is the alerted service but is only a symptom; the fix is in payment or its flag.
A 50% payment-failure flag fits the roughly 30% checkout error ratio and the fast-failing payment errors. The flag is the leading candidate for the cause, though its onset time is not verified.
Kafka publish failures are not the cause: no kafka client-span error series appeared.

root_causes.cause: Charge requests fail about half the time with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. loyalty_level=gold', consistent with the flagd flag paymentFailure being ON at the 50% variant. Payment has no rollout change, so the flag is the likely source.

diagnosis.summary: ErrorBudgetBurn on checkout (30.5% errors) is caused by failing PaymentService/Charge calls. Checkout's only erroring client dependency is payment, and payment's own server spans fail at the same rate, quickly (p95 about 2 ms). Payment's pods are healthy and have no rollout changes. The only flag switched on is paymentFailure at 50%, which fits the observed error rate, but its switch-on time is not in the data, so the onset link is unconfirmed. Checkout is the alerted service, but the fix belongs in payment (or flagd's paymentFailure flag).

alternatives.why_not: Payment and checkout each have one rollout revision (15:25Z), with no release near the 15:40Z alert, so there is no bad revision to roll back to.
Payment's pods are healthy and the failures come from flag evaluation, so a restart would not change the error rate.
Errors are fast, deterministic rejections (about 2 ms), not capacity saturation, so more replicas would not reduce them.

plan.no_action_reason: Root cause is likely the flagd flag paymentFailure being ON at 50%, which no available action can change. A human should set it OFF (or 0%) in flagd if it is not an intended experiment, and confirm the switch-on time. If the flag is off, investigate the payment token-validation path for gold users.
plan.summary: No automated action is proposed, because the likely cause is the paymentFailure flag in flagd, and none of rollout_undo, restart or scale can fix it. A human should disable the flag after confirming it is intentional, and confirm its switch-on time.

inferences.statement: checkout is relaying payment's rejection: its PlaceOrder and Charge client spans and frontend's 422 responses carry the same token message, so checkout is a victim.
The failure is inside payment's token check, not in a downstream dependency, since the deepest error span is payment Charge with no failing child.
A new payment deployment did not cause this incident, since the only revision predates the alert by about 15 minutes and is unchanged.

root_causes.cause: Token validation rejects requests on the loyalty_level=gold path, most likely because the paymentFailure flag (ENABLED, 50% variant) injects failures into Charge. Not yet confirmed that the flag changed near 15:39Z.

Less likely alternative: a payment token or secret configuration problem, not a flag, that rejects valid gold-tier tokens. No payment rollout changed, so this would need a config or secret change outside the rollout history.

diagnosis.summary: payment (the alerted service) is failing about 30% of Charge requests with 'Payment request failed. Invalid token. demo.user_context.loyalty_level=gold'. The failures are fast (p95 fell from about 43 ms to about 2 ms), and the failing path is inside payment's token check, not a dependency. Checkout's and frontend's errors are relayed from payment, so checkout is a victim. No payment rollout changed near the alert. The leading candidate is the enabled paymentFailure flag (50%), but its ON time is not confirmed, and the 30.5% ratio is below 50%, which suggests the errors are limited to a subset of traffic such as gold-tier users.

alternatives.why_not: payment has a single revision (15:25:43Z, no change-cause, ev_215abb33382ee438) and nothing changed near the 15:38Z onset, so there is no bad release to roll back to.
The errors are a deliberate token rejection tied to the flag state, not a stuck process; a restart would leave the flag on and the errors would return.
Failures are fast (p95 fell from 43 ms to 2 ms) and not capacity-related, so more replicas would not reduce the error ratio.

plan.no_action_reason: Root cause is most likely the paymentFailure flag (ev_6316761300f3f7f7, ev_d7b4d4ef26df5300), which is not an action here. Human: check flagd history for when it was enabled and disable it if not intended for lab. Confirm whether the 50% variant is scoped to loyalty_level=gold, and verify no token secret or config changed (ev_417bce900721237b).
plan.summary: No automated action is supported: the failures track the enabled paymentFailure flag (50% variant), not a payment release, and the flag is outside the actions I can take. A human should confirm the flag's ON time in flagd and switch paymentFailure off, which should stop the Charge errors on payment and clear the relayed checkout and frontend errors.
